claim_verdicts.evidence: Page carries feature-state stable for_k8s_version v1.30 and says: "Validating admission policies offer a declarative, in-process alternative to validating admission webhooks." admission-controllers.md: "ValidatingAdmissionPolicy provides a way to embed declarative validation code within the API, without relying on any external HTTP callouts." Stable since 1.30, so present in 1.34.

"spec.validations contains CEL expressions ... If an expression evaluates to false, the validation check is enforced" and "For each admission request, the API server evaluates CEL expressions of each (policy, binding, param) combination that match the request. For a request to be admitted it must pass **all** evaluations."

"CEL is non-Turing complete and offers a variety of production safety controls to limit execution time." "All CEL expressions evaluated by Kubernetes are constrained by a runtime cost budget ... If the CEL interpreter executes too many instructions, the runtime cost budget will be exceeded, execution of the expressions will be halted, and an error will result."

"At least a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and a corresponding ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding must be defined for a policy to have an effect." Validation actions: "Deny: Validation failure results in a denied request. Warn: Validation failure is reported to the request client as a warning. Audit: Validation failure is included in the audit event for the API request."

Docs: "Deny: Validation failure results in a denied request"; admission controllers intercept requests "prior to persistence". Captured output at stage-3: "The pods \"api-by-tag\" is invalid: : ValidatingAdmissionPolicy 'require-image-digest' with binding 'require-image-digest' denied request: an image from ghcr.io/duyan11110/ must be named by digest (@sha256:...)" — the validation's message is carried.

"Admission controllers apply to requests that create, delete, or modify objects. ... do not (and cannot) block requests to read." Dry-run: "any relevant admission controllers are run ... The changes are not persisted". Round 2: s4 and q5 now say "Admission checks requests that create, update or delete an object, before anything is stored; it never looks back at objects already stored", matching the round-1 suggested_text.

"CEL expressions have access to the contents of the Admission request/response, organized into CEL variables": object, oldObject, request, params, namespaceObject, authorizer. admission-controllers.md: VAP embeds validation "without relying on any external HTTP callouts." No variable or library exposes a registry; inability to resolve a digest or signature follows.

"Admission webhooks are HTTP callbacks that receive admission requests and do something with them ... Mutating admission webhooks ... can modify objects ... validating admission webhooks are invoked and can reject requests"; for url config: "The scheme must be \"https\""; service form is https://<name>.<namespace>.svc. The server is user-written ("Write an admission webhook server").

"Ignore means that an error calling the webhook is ignored and the API request is allowed to continue. Fail means that an error calling the webhook causes the admission to fail and the API request to be rejected." Applies to "Network errors, timeouts, or connection failures when contacting the webhook" and non-2xx/malformed responses.

"failurePolicy defines how mis-configurations and CEL expressions evaluating to error from the admission policy are handled." "A validation that evaluates to false is always enforced according to these actions. Failures defined by the failurePolicy are enforced according to these actions only if the failurePolicy is set to Fail (or not specified), otherwise the failures are ignored."

git show stage-3:deploy/gitops/config-repo/platform/policies/require-image-digest.yaml: failurePolicy: Fail; rules apiGroups [""], apiVersions ["v1"], operations ["CREATE","UPDATE"], resources ["pods"] (no deployments: a Deployment is not matched; Pods its ReplicaSet creates are CREATE requests on pods); expression over object.spec.containers; binding Deny, namespaceSelector kubernetes.io/metadata.name: donhang. Excerpt lines 14-38 match.

kubernetes.io/metadata.name — "The Kubernetes API server (part of the control plane) sets this label on all namespaces. The label value is set to the name of the namespace. You can't change this label's value. This is useful if you want to target a specific namespace with a label selector."

API reference HTTP requests have no namespace segment: "POST /apis/admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1/validatingadmissionpolicies" and "POST /apis/admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1/validatingadmissionpolicybindings", "PUT .../validatingadmissionpolicybindings/{name}" — both kinds are cluster-scoped.

Lesson excerpt lines 37-61 match character for character.

"When you set ?dryRun=All, any relevant admission controllers are run, validating admission controllers check the request post-mutation ... The changes are not persisted to the underlying storage"; "Kubernetes guarantees that dry-run requests will not be persisted in storage or have any other side effects." Dry run applies to POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE (replace = PUT = update).

git grep at stage-3: deploy/gateway-api/standard-install.yaml L20065 "kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy", L20070 name "safe-upgrades.gateway.networking.k8s.io", L20102 "kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding", L20109 policyName: safe-upgrades.gateway.networking.k8s.io; the policy has two validations (messages at L20085, L20096), matching VALIDATIONS 2 in the output.

Staging overlay: all six ghcr.io/duyan11110/ images (incl. migrate, notifications-migrate, payments-migrate) carry digest: sha256:... . Hooks (base/migrate-hook.yaml, notifications.yaml, payments.yaml) are Pods with argocd.argoproj.io/hook: Sync and restartPolicy: Never, so they finish and are not phase Running. deploy-verified.sh verifies the digest, then commits "$registry/donhang-api:$tag@$api".

Docker docs: "Tags are mutable, meaning anyone with push access to a registry can overwrite a tag silently, so a reference you reviewed last week may point to different content today. Digests are immutable." deploy-verified.sh usage line at stage-3: "default: try 1.0.0, which is refused" (verify-image.sh fails on it).

Pod Security Standards control table lists HostProcess, Host Namespaces, Privileged Containers, Capabilities, HostPath Volumes, Host Ports, AppArmor, SELinux, /proc Mount Type, Seccomp, Sysctls, Volume Types, Privilege Escalation, Running as Non-root, Running as Non-root user; Grep for "image" or "registry" in the page finds no match.

Round 2 text: "Đơn Hàng runs none that checks images on staging". At stage-3 the only webhook configurations are cert-manager's (scripts/k8s/cert-manager-install.sh, cluster donhang) and MetalLB's; neither checks images, and no policy engine exists. Signatures are verified only by deploy-verified.sh before commit.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Conditional recommendation ("Fail fits when an unchecked Pod is worse than a stalled deploy, Ignore when the reverse holds"), stated with its condition; kind opinion, no source required.

issues.text: New in round 2 (changed paragraph). Read literally, admission does not skip running Pods: an update to a running Pod goes through admission, which is what the next clause relies on. The point is that admission never re-checks stored objects on its own.
issues.quote: Since admission skips running Pods, the loop takes each Pod in `donhang` whose `status.phase` is `Running`
issues.fix: Write: "Since admission never looks back at stored Pods, the loop takes each Pod in `donhang` whose `status.phase` is `Running`..."

issues.quote: Since admission skips running Pods, the loop takes each Pod in `donhang` whose `status.phase` is `Running` and sends it back unchanged with `kubectl replace --dry-run=server`: the API server admits it as an update, runs the policy
issues.text: New in round 2 (changed paragraph). 'admission skips running Pods' and, a few words later, 'the API server admits it as an update, runs the policy' on that same running Pod read as a contradiction; I had to go back to section 4 ('never looks back at objects already stored') to reconcile them.
issues.fix: Reuse section 4's wording: replace 'Since admission skips running Pods' with 'Since admission never looks back at Pods already stored'.
